title: observational comparative study: Intravitreal treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) and diabetic macular edema (DME) with a bispecific antibody Vabysmo® (faricimab) vs. a classical anti-VEGF inhibitor Eylea® (aflibercept) in a treat-and-extend-regimen (FATE).
summary:
Since the approval of the first injection therapy for the eye diseases diabetic macular edema and wet age-related macular degeneration, the prognosis for vision has improved significantly. Today, injection therapy is the first-line treatment for these diseases. Since the first drug, others with similar effects have been approved. One of these drugs is aflibercept (registered trade name: Eylea®). In addition to the choice of drug, the therapy can be individualized by adjusting the intervals between injections. The latter is done in the treatment according to the so-called treat-and-extend regimen. Before each injection, the retina is examined and in case of dry findings, the injection interval is extended by two weeks. If there is an increase or new fluid, the interval between injections is shortened by two weeks. Treatment is considered complete only if the retina remains dry for sixteen weeks without an injection. This extention of intervals reflects the chronic aspect of the disease, as even a dry retina may not be a healthy retina.
In January 2022, a new drug containing the active compound faricimab (trade name: Vabysmo®) was approved in the United States for the treatment of the eye diseases mentioned above. Approval in the UK and Japan was followed by approval in the EU by the European Medicines Agency in September 2022. This drug inhibits the formation of new vessels and fluid leakage in the retina in two ways, unlike the other drugs. In the pivotal studies, it was shown that in a majority of patients, the interval between injections could be extended to an interval of 12-16 weeks without more frequent adverse events or side effects. Thus, a significantly less frequent stay for injection therapy was required during the course of treatment.
We intend to test whether this advantage is also reflected in daily use.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Consenting patients with macular edema, with underlying cause: neovascular age-related macular degeneration, diabetes mellitus-related maculopathy.
Minimum age 18 years, gender male/female/diverse.
Exclusion criteria:
Macular edema caused or influenced by an underlying cause other than neovascular age-related macular degeneration or diabetes mellitus-related maculopathy.
lack of capacity to consent.
